quest.title: Into the Hinterland
quest.description: With the mechanical crab as your guide, it is time to head to the contaminated region.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here! This should be... Huh? Where's the crab?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did it secretly scuttle away?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The traps weren't triggered, so it should still be here... Odd...

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kuli...

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's here!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You honored our agreement and waited here until we returned.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As such, I'll hold up my end and give you another mechanical part. Keep it safe. I'm not giving you another one if you lose it.

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Glad you're satisfied. If you want more mechanical parts, take us deeper into the contaminated region.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I want to see what happened there — what caused the Avidya Forest to become like this.

talks.objective: Set off for the contaminated region

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the contaminated region that everyone's been talking about... It definitely looks different from normal!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's like... really creepy and suffocating...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Do you feel unwell at all?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Doing fine so far.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Good. It's as I predicted: Elemental power confers a degree of resistance against the contaminated region's influence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How do you know that?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I haven't entered the contaminated region for a proper investigation, but I've conducted quite a few controlled experiments.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: My observations during our time here have all but confirmed my hypothesis. Look at these flowers. How are they different from normal?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: This flower species is formally known as the "Sumeru Rose," but it is also known as the "Ley Line Lodestar."

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: They're sensitive to Ley Lines and emit varying amounts of light in response. Excessive brightness indicates a dangerous level of Ley Line activity in the surrounding area.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: From the looks of things, the Ley Lines around here are already out of control.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're saying that the contamination here is coming from Ley Lines?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I can't confirm that right now, but I think that is the case.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Let's take another look around and see if we can discover more clues.

talks.objective: Head toward the depths of the contaminated region

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know, we haven't seen any animals this entire time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The birds used to chirp really loudly, and there were a lot of foxes...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The contaminated region currently appears to have a critical efflux of Ley Line energy, which is probably the root cause of the patients' cognitive disturbances.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Some animals have keen awareness. They sensed something abnormal in this area and fled.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Leaky Ley Lines sure can cause a lot of damage, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Like how plants have preferred growth conditions, we also gradually habituate to our surrounding environment.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Climate, temperature, humidity, intensity of Ley Line energies. When people live under fixed conditions, they reach a sort of "homeostasis" with their environment.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This equilibrium is broken when the surrounding environment abruptly changes, causing people's bodies to react in abnormal ways.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If normal fluctuations in temperature occur, then our bodies automatically adjust. However, the average person cannot adapt to changes in Ley Line energy, and so they fall ill.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ah, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then why are we okay?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #I'm not sure why you are, but {NICKNAME} and I are fine because our elemental capabilities allow us to adapt to this kind of change.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Of course, it's not a good idea to spend too much time in areas with concentrated Ley Line energy. The only one who can freely traverse this place is probably the mechanical crab.

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's about it for the investigation. Help me find an open space. I want to test something.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Environment... No wind... Target parameters... Normal...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Setup complete. Excellent — looks like it's working.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: A Purification Device I made. It can absorb excess Ley Line energy and temporarily stabilize an area.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a neat thing! Let's set up more and cover the entire region!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I wouldn't mind if that would actually work. Unfortunately, once this "contamination" is present, it isn't something that a few Purification Devices can fix.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Purification Devices have their limits. At best, they can only prevent the contaminated region from expanding temporarily.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If we want to permanently eradicate the contamination from the Ley Line effluence, we'll need to tackle the source.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: At the heart of the contaminated region?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? The mechanical crab is acting a little strange.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Something's approaching...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: So that's it. Now that the Ley Line energy has stabilized, the monsters that had left are starting to return.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Get rid of them quickly! Don't let them get close to the Purification Device!

talks.objective: Catch up with the Mechanical Crab

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... That's all of them.

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, where are you— Wait for us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Let's hurry and keep up, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: Aaah... Spare me, please spare me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: These injuries are superficial. Don't move. I'll patch you up.

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: Who are you all? What happened to those mechanical monsters?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we took care of them!

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: Good. Haha... That's good...

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: Aaah, it's a monster! Hurry, attack it!

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How do we explain this? Crabby here isn't a bad guy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It heard you shouting for help and brought us here to rescue you.

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: It's faking it — it has to be! Maybe it's gonna partner up with the other mechanical monsters and kill me!

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: Do you know what's inside the forest? It's all... It's all crawling with mechanical freaks!

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: I just came here to pick herbs, but I accidentally went into the contaminated region and almost died.

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: I gotta get out of here. Yes... Yes, I have to escape...

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: Be careful. These mechanical life forms are up to no good. It'd be best if you stayed far, far away from them!

dialogues.speaker: Jasar
dialogues.text: No wonder the Akademiya wanted to completely ban the existence of mechanical life forms. Those things should be annihilated...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: His inarticulate speech and bodily tremors indicate psyche disruption. He's been inside the contaminated region for too long.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We've purified the Ley Line energy over there. Follow this path out and you'll soon see the village.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: When he gets to the village, someone will bring him to Collei for help. I already prepared medication that will return him to normal.

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Hmm... So you think you did a "good job" and want a part as your reward?

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kolu!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's so hard to understand...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Alright, regardless of what you're thinking, you did some real good this time.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: That's why I'll give you another mechanical part. Need any help with it?

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kelukulo.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Guess not. Well, make sure to hang on to it. What was going through your owner's mind when he made you, I wonder? You're like a giant mechanical crab on the outside and a fluffy little hamster on the inside.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: And also, how do you feel about that person saying that you're as evil as the other mechanical life forms?

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kulilu?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, it definitely doesn't understand you.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: It seems like it possesses limited understanding only towards matters related to mechanical components.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: "Help others to get parts." That's probably its thought process. As for why it — rather, its owner — is collecting so many components, I'm not sure.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: It's getting late. Let's set up camp for the night. We'll explore further tomorrow after a night's rest.

talks.objective: Look for a spot to set up a tent

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let's set up camp here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Paimon also thinks it's a good spot!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh? Any particular reason?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This place is perfect to put up a big tent!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We can also set up a cooking pot and cook tons of delicious food!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A very Paimon reason.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You're not wrong, but the primary reason for choosing this place is because its higher elevation keeps us away from the water vapor below.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Rainforests are very wet. You should always be careful when spending the night in damp places.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: For the next tasks at hand, let's divide and conquer. I'll set up the tent, you'll be in charge of making the fire, and Paimon will forage for edibles nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Leave it to Paimon! Paimon's a pro!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm not expecting that much. Just do what you can.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Thanks to Tighnari's guidance, you safely start a fire...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's right. You can use rushes to start a fire in the wilderness.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Their piths are relatively dry and can be readily set aflame. The downside is that they produce a lot of smoke.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #*sob* {NICKNAME}, Tighnari... Paimon couldn't find any food.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't know that rainforests had so many interesting plants until we came here! There were all sorts of weird-looking mushrooms, but Paimon didn't know which ones were edible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon also saw wild berries on the ground, and Paimon was gonna fly over and pick them up, but the dead leaves on top suddenly started moving! It freaked Paimon out!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Those were probably Deadleaf Butterflies. They camouflage as dead leaves to evade predators.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: My guess is that they mistook you for a bird when you flew over, so they fled. Little did they know that you were more scared than they were.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Never mind. The tent's up, so you two go rest. I'll forage for food.

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh? You found some already.

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kolu!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon understands it this time! It wants mechanical parts again!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Sorry, no part this time.

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kulilu?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: That task wasn't important enough. If every little thing resulted in a reward, then it might start to take advantage of the system.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I'll note little things like this and give a cumulative reward at a later time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you running low on parts...?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Ahem, that is one reason.

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kuli...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It looks really sad...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: ...After some further thought, it might come up with some weird misunderstanding if I don't give it something. Alright, here's another for you.

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kolu!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I'm off to prepare dinner. We'll take shifts on lookout duty tonight. You two can sleep first. I'll wake you up later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We need lookouts?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Even though most animals fled because of the Ley Lines, we can't completely let down our guard.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: It's settled, then. I'll set up some pest-repelling devices so poisonous insects don't come crawling into the tent.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Have a good night. Not too good, though.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey!

talks.objective: Go into the tent to rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's getting sleepy... Ah! Is this because of the Ley Lines?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a while since we camped outside like this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe... This feels like when we just started adventuring together! Nighty night! {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Paimon gradually falls asleep while reminiscing...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hm? You're awake earlier than I expected. Did you sleep well?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: That's good. I was worried that you two wouldn't be able to sleep, so I used two of my homemade incenses.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Don't worry, they're made from all-natural ingredients. They have a light fragrance and aren't harmful to the body.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Speaking of which, have you seen the crab?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: It was scampering around over there just now, but I don't know where it went.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you wary of it?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: So you can tell. My suspicion is less towards the crab, and more directed to its unrevealed owner.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: A Ley Line effluence of this magnitude occurred without any warning. Someone probably disrupted the natural flow of the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Until we fully understand the situation, take extra caution. The Akademiya has banned mechanical life form research for years, so the origin of these creatures is very suspect.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Topics related to mechanical life forms were popular in the Spantamad for a time. Some of my juniors had also thrown themselves into such research.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: They proposed an intriguing idea: Use our knowledge to create a "new and practical" life form that could help humanity "conquer nature."

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: However, no matter which modules or parts are installed, a machine is innately a construct that receives and executes commands. They can never possess self-awareness like us or other living organisms.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: In their pursuit to discover the differences between mechanical and biological life forms, zealous researchers performed unregulated vivisections and other absurdly cruel experiments on animals. Research on mechanical life forms was thus banned.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: The irony is that the researchers became even more impetuous afterward. Who knows, maybe the subject will be unbanned in a few years.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you not like this area of research?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Hmm... That's a difficult question to answer.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I'm interested in the topic of mechanical life, but I don't like the researchers' attitudes.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: It's just my personal opinion.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: My ancestors and the Valuka Shuna of the desert coexisted together and supported one another. The bloodline of my people was born from this symbiotic relationship.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: So to me, all life is important. To understand life, you must first respect it.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Life is not an expendable commodity, and knowledge should not be wielded like a scepter. These are the points of contention I have with some researchers, and why I left the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Once you start placing yourself above other life forms, I mean... What kind of results do you expect to get from researching pure life with impure intentions?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I understand what you mean.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Really? Well, I'm glad to hear it.

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kuli...

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kolu!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Coffee? Did you prepare this for us?

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kolu!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It looks like it wants a reward again...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Alright, seeing that you're working so hard to help out, I'll give you another part.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: You're not planning on using it? Many of your own parts are critically degraded, and you're running low on power.

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kelukulo.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #Alright, suit yourself. Oh and thanks for the coffee, but I'm about to go to sleep. Leave it with {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: The night watch is yours. Stay safe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #S—Sorry, {NICKNAME}, Paimon slept through the entire night...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? You're not mad?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #Good morning, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Quick question, do you feel off at all?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm a little dizzy.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Me too. The farther in we go, the closer we get to the source of the Ley Line effluence. We'll be heading out earlier today. I'll take down the tent.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is there something we can do?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Extinguish our fire so we don't set the entire forest aflame.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Also, retrieve the pest-repelling devices from last night. We don't want to affect the ecosystem here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it! Paimon will take care of the fire!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll retrieve the pest-repelling devices.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Alright. Let's meet back here later.

choices.text: Your punishment is solo watch duty.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe. Don't worry, Paimon will be sure to stay awake next time!

choices.text: Because the "conquest of nature" is bad?
The Akademiya previously conducted research on mechanical life forms?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: You have to maintain constant vigilance in dangerous places like this. Yawning all the time like that is no good.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: If you can't stay awake, it's okay. Go sleep some more. I'm not tired yet.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can manage.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Really? You don't need to push yourself. I'm used to staying up all night because many plant and animal species can only be observed during nighttime.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hm? You're still awake?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Last night's pest-repelling devices are recovered...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, it's about time to head out. As we go further in, we may encounter more berserk machines.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The effects of the Ley Lines will also increase. If you're struggling, it would be wise to avoid conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Try to conserve as much energy as possible until we reach the source of the contamination.

talks.objective: Go to the depths of the contaminated region

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Guess it'll have to wait until we return.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I also just remembered that I forgot to apply essential oil to my tail. You probably noticed that it isn't as glossy as usual.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Nope, I don't see it.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hmm... Perhaps one night doesn't make too much of a difference.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'll make a new blend when we get back. It should make up for last night. I should have some leftover herbs from last month...

talks.objective: Defeat the monsters in your path

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How do you put out a fire...?

dialogues.speaker: Yara
dialogues.text: Thank you. I feel much better now.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I can do this. I can do this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Now that the fire's out, we just need to pack up the cooking pot...

dialogues.speaker: Asha
dialogues.text: (Murmuring to herself, Asha seems to be praying for her son's recovery.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The mechanical crab went that way. Let's keep up!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hey! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Come on you big lummox, raise your head and look up!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As I thought. The closer we get to the contamination's source, the more mechanical monsters that appear...
